      "title": "Team admin/owner check uses AND instead of OR",
      "body": "The variable `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed with `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`. This requires a user to be both a team admin and a team owner simultaneously to pass. In Cal.com, team admins and team owners are distinct roles; most admins are not owners and vice versa. As a result, authorized team admins (or owners) who are not both will be denied when they are not the organizer or an attendee, breaking the add guests feature for team bookings. The condition should use `||` not `&&`."

      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Uses current user's credentials instead of organizer's for calendar updates",
      "body": "The handler creates `EventManager` with `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials: [...credentials] })`, where `user` is the session user and `credentials` come from `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`. When a team admin, attendee, or anyone other than the booking organizer adds guests, the calendar update will be attempted using the requester's credentials, not the organizer's. This can fail to update the organizer's calendar or update the wrong calendar, leaving invitees without proper calendar invitations. The EventManager should be constructed with the booking organizer's credentials (or team members' credentials), not the current user's."
    },

      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Passes raw `guests` instead of `uniqueGuests` to email function",
      "body": "`sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` is called with the raw input array `guests`, not the filtered `uniqueGuests`. `guests` may contain emails that were filtered out (already existing attendees or blacklisted). Inside `sendAddGuestsEmails`, the logic decides whether to send `AttendeeScheduledEmail` or `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail` based on `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)`. If an existing attendee's email was in the raw input but was not actually added, they will incorrectly receive a full `AttendeeScheduledEmail` (the standard booking confirmation) instead of the 'new guests added' notification. The function should receive the actual newly added email list (`uniqueGuests`)."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/emails/email-manager.ts",
      "line": 525,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "New guest emails ignore event type email disable settings",
      "body": "`sendAddGuestsEmails` does not accept `eventTypeMetadata` and does not call `eventTypeDisableHostEmail` or `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail`, unlike other email functions such as `sendScheduledEmails` or `sendLocationChangeEmails`. As a result, even when an event type has host or attendee standard emails disabled, this function will still send organizer and attendee add-guests emails. Users who opted out of email notifications will receive unwanted emails. The function should respect the event type's email disable flags."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts",
      "line": 26,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Does not check booking status before allowing guest additions",
      "body": "The handler fetches the booking but never validates `booking.status`. A cancelled or rejected booking can still have new attendees added via the API, leading to emails and calendar updates for a non-active event. The UI hides the action for cancelled bookings, but the API remains open. The handler should reject adding guests to bookings with statuses like CANCELLED, REJECTED, or any terminal status."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts",
      "line": 58,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "`booking.userId` may be null for team bookings causing findFirstOrThrow failure",
      "body": "`const organizer = await prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } });` assumes `booking.userId` is always set. For team events (especially collective or round robin where the booking may not be assigned to a single user), `booking.userId` can be null. The fallback `|| 0` queries for a user with id 0, which does not exist and throws an error, causing the entire mutation to fail. The organizer should be determined using `booking.eventType?.userId` or the included `booking.user` relation, with appropriate handling for null."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts",
      "line": 5,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Server-side schema allows duplicate guest emails",
      "body": "The schema defines `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` but does not enforce that the array is non-empty or that emails within the array are unique. Client-side validation in `AddGuestsDialog` prevents duplicates for normal UI usage, but a direct API request can send duplicates. The handler filters against existing attendees only, not within the input, so duplicate attendee records with the same email can be created in the database. The schema should use `.min(1)` and a uniqueness refinement, or the handler should deduplicate the input."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts",
      "line": 165,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Passes stale pre-update booking object to updateCalendarAttendees",
      "body": "`await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` uses the `booking` object fetched before the attendee update. If `updateCalendarAttendees` relies on `booking.attendees` to determine which attendees are new or removed, it will operate on the old attendee list while `evt.attendees` contains the updated list. This can result in incorrect calendar invitations (e.g., not sending invitations to newly added guests or sending updates to removed ones). The updated booking object (returned by `prisma.booking.update`) should be passed instead, or the method should be verified to only use `evt.attendees`."
    },
    {
      "file": "apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx",
      "line": 42,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Error message fallback never used due to template literal always truthy",
      "body": "In `onError`, `const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`;` always produces a string, even if `err.data?.code` and `err.message` are undefined (resulting in \"undefined: undefined\"). Therefore the later condition `message || t(\"unable_to_add_guests\")` never uses the fallback translation. The error toast can show a confusing or misleading message. The fallback should be applied before constructing the string, or use a conditional that checks the presence of actual data."
    }
  ]

findings.title: Team admin/owner check uses AND instead of OR
findings.body: The variable `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed with `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`. This requires a user to be both a team admin and a team owner simultaneously to pass. In Cal.com, team admins and team owners are distinct roles; most admins are not owners and vice versa. As a result, authorized team admins (or owners) who are not both will be denied when they are not the organizer or an attendee, breaking the add guests feature for team bookings. The condition should use `||` not `&&`.

findings.title: Uses current user's credentials instead of organizer's for calendar updates
findings.body: The handler creates `EventManager` with `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials: [...credentials] })`, where `user` is the session user and `credentials` come from `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`. When a team admin, attendee, or anyone other than the booking organizer adds guests, the calendar update will be attempted using the requester's credentials, not the organizer's. This can fail to update the organizer's calendar or update the wrong calendar, leaving invitees without proper calendar invitations. The EventManager should be constructed with the booking organizer's credentials (or team members' credentials), not the current user's.

findings.title: Passes raw `guests` instead of `uniqueGuests` to email function
findings.body: `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` is called with the raw input array `guests`, not the filtered `uniqueGuests`. `guests` may contain emails that were filtered out (already existing attendees or blacklisted). Inside `sendAddGuestsEmails`, the logic decides whether to send `AttendeeScheduledEmail` or `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail` based on `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)`. If an existing attendee's email was in the raw input but was not actually added, they will incorrectly receive a full `AttendeeScheduledEmail` (the standard booking confirmation) instead of the 'new guests added' notification. The function should receive the actual newly added email list (`uniqueGuests`).

findings.title: New guest emails ignore event type email disable settings
findings.body: `sendAddGuestsEmails` does not accept `eventTypeMetadata` and does not call `eventTypeDisableHostEmail` or `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail`, unlike other email functions such as `sendScheduledEmails` or `sendLocationChangeEmails`. As a result, even when an event type has host or attendee standard emails disabled, this function will still send organizer and attendee add-guests emails. Users who opted out of email notifications will receive unwanted emails. The function should respect the event type's email disable flags.

findings.title: Does not check booking status before allowing guest additions
findings.body: The handler fetches the booking but never validates `booking.status`. A cancelled or rejected booking can still have new attendees added via the API, leading to emails and calendar updates for a non-active event. The UI hides the action for cancelled bookings, but the API remains open. The handler should reject adding guests to bookings with statuses like CANCELLED, REJECTED, or any terminal status.

findings.title: `booking.userId` may be null for team bookings causing findFirstOrThrow failure
findings.body: `const organizer = await prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } });` assumes `booking.userId` is always set. For team events (especially collective or round robin where the booking may not be assigned to a single user), `booking.userId` can be null. The fallback `|| 0` queries for a user with id 0, which does not exist and throws an error, causing the entire mutation to fail. The organizer should be determined using `booking.eventType?.userId` or the included `booking.user` relation, with appropriate handling for null.

findings.title: Server-side schema allows duplicate guest emails
findings.body: The schema defines `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` but does not enforce that the array is non-empty or that emails within the array are unique. Client-side validation in `AddGuestsDialog` prevents duplicates for normal UI usage, but a direct API request can send duplicates. The handler filters against existing attendees only, not within the input, so duplicate attendee records with the same email can be created in the database. The schema should use `.min(1)` and a uniqueness refinement, or the handler should deduplicate the input.

findings.title: Passes stale pre-update booking object to updateCalendarAttendees
findings.body: `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` uses the `booking` object fetched before the attendee update. If `updateCalendarAttendees` relies on `booking.attendees` to determine which attendees are new or removed, it will operate on the old attendee list while `evt.attendees` contains the updated list. This can result in incorrect calendar invitations (e.g., not sending invitations to newly added guests or sending updates to removed ones). The updated booking object (returned by `prisma.booking.update`) should be passed instead, or the method should be verified to only use `evt.attendees`.

findings.title: Error message fallback never used due to template literal always truthy
findings.body: In `onError`, `const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`;` always produces a string, even if `err.data?.code` and `err.message` are undefined (resulting in "undefined: undefined"). Therefore the later condition `message || t("unable_to_add_guests")` never uses the fallback translation. The error toast can show a confusing or misleading message. The fallback should be applied before constructing the string, or use a conditional that checks the presence of actual data.
